transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because sometimes, usually at night after work or if dinner’s been tense, I start eating and it feels like I lose control. Like I’m watching myself keep reaching for more food, but I can’t make myself stop.
During those times, do you eat what most people would consider an unusually large amount of food?
Yeah. On bad nights I’ll eat a full plate of leftovers, then keep picking through bread, snacks, ice cream—within an hour or two. It’s way more than I’d eat if anyone else were there.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?

Yes. Sometimes after everyone’s asleep, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Other times I take laxatives, telling myself I’m just undoing the damage. I feel pretty embarrassed afterward, and shaky.
How often do these binge-and-purge episodes happen?
For the last few months, it’s been most weeks—usually one night where I lose control eating, then I try to make up for it afterward.
Does your body shape or weight have a big effect on how you feel about yourself?

Yeah, it does. If my cashier shirt pulls a little at my stomach, I spend the whole shift feeling like customers can tell I have no discipline. How I feel about myself depends way too much on how I look that day.
Are you currently at a significantly low body weight for your height?
I’m not really sure what counts as significantly low. I don’t think of myself as underweight, though.
Has a doctor or anyone else told you that you are underweight?
No, nobody has told me that. I haven’t had anyone say my weight is too low.
Have these binge-and-purge episodes been happening at least once a week for the past 3 months?
Yeah. For the last few months, most weeks I’ve had at least one night where eating feels out of control, and then I try to make up for it afterward.
